summary.intent: Fix a broken Slack notification in the e2e triage GitHub Action and add an early 'triage started' notification so users know the process has begun.
summary.outcome: Shipped fixes across multiple pushes: improved Slack error logging, collapsed the per-agent matrix into a single triage job, fixed a job-level env var bug blocking the start notification, and normalized a malformed thread_ts (missing decimal point) that was causing INT64 overflow errors. Two config-side issues (bot channel invite) were left to the user.

repo: e2e-triage.yml and e2e.yml use two different Slack auth mechanisms: e2e.yml posts via E2E_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL (incoming webhook, 'CLI E2E Failures' app), while e2e-triage.yml uses SLACK_BOT_TOKEN with chat.postMessage — the bot must be separately invited to the channel (webhook 'integration' add does not add the bot user).

The triage workflow originally ran one Claude Code session per matrix agent; collapsing failed agents into a single job/session was intentional so cross-agent failures sharing a root cause can be correlated instead of independently rediscovered per agent.

e2e-fix.yml downloads triage output artifacts; when the matrix was collapsed, artifact naming changed from per-agent (e2e-plan-${agent}) to a single e2e-triage artifact, requiring e2e-fix.yml's download step and prompt to be updated in lockstep.

Slack thread_ts values must be preserved as strings (e.g. '1774295548.366959'); something upstream (likely GitHub Actions workflow_dispatch input handling or a dispatching Cloudflare Worker) strips the decimal point, turning it into a huge integer that overflows Slack's parser to INT64_MAX.

code.finding: Original script checked Slack response .ok but only logged 'non-ok response' without the JSON error field, making failures like not_in_channel undiagnosable from CI logs; fixed to log the error field and full response body.
Per-agent 'Post triage started' step lived inside the triage matrix job; removed in favor of one consolidated notification in matrix-setup/setup job.

SLACK_BOT_TOKEN was set at step-level env, but the step's `if:` condition referencing env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN is evaluated before step-level env is applied, causing the condition to silently see an empty string; fix moves the token to job-level env.
Added sed-based normalization to insert a missing decimal point into thread_ts (e.g. 1774295548366959 -> 1774295548.366959) before using it in Slack API calls.

workflow: GitHub Actions `${{ inputs.foo }}` expressions are template-expanded into shell text before execution and are injectable if not passed via env vars — prefer `env:` + `$VAR` in `run:` blocks over direct `${{ }}` interpolation, even for low-risk workflow_dispatch inputs.

When debugging a 'successful' CI run that has a hidden failure, check step-level conclusions/logs (not just job-level status) — Slack's API returns HTTP 200 even on failure, so curl -fsS-style status checks won't catch it; must inspect the JSON body's `ok`/`error` fields.

friction: Initial CI run showed all jobs as 'success' even though 3 Slack notifications silently failed, requiring step-level log digging to find the real error.
First fix introduced a new bug (if: condition couldn't see step-scoped env var), so the 'Post triage starting' notification still didn't appear after the first push.
Second fix surfaced a different failure (not_in_channel) that required distinguishing between two separate Slack auth mechanisms (webhook vs bot token) already in use in different workflows.

After fixing not_in_channel, a third issue appeared: thread_ts arriving without its decimal point, causing a Slack INT64 overflow error — required a WebSearch into Slack's ts format docs to confirm the string format requirement.
User had to submit two screenshots of failing GitHub Actions runs to get the assistant enough detail to diagnose issues.
A planned change (making 'Post triage starting' its own top-level job) was later dropped/superseded once the more pressing thread_ts bug was found.
open_items: User needs to invite the Slack bot associated with SLACK_BOT_TOKEN into #project-troy (e.g. via /invite @CLI E2E Failures) since adding the webhook integration alone doesn't add the bot user.
Verify on the next triage run that Slack notifications (start, completion, fix plan) all succeed end-to-end now that thread_ts normalization is in place.
Confirm whether 'Post triage starting' should still become its own top-level job for Actions UI visibility, or if that idea was permanently shelved in favor of the setup-job placement.
